channel.title: Riddim Yard
channel.description:
Riddim Yard is the home of foundation Jamaican music: Ska, Rocksteady, Deejay, Dub, Roots & Dancehall 
 
email: rickhowe@riddimyard.com.au

item.title: Too Too Bad
item.description:
Riddim Yard's favourite current artist Lila Iké opens the show with 'What It Feels Like', her outstanding cut on Protoje's Feel It Riddim. Following her GRAMMY-nominated album Treasure Self Love - Riddim Yard's album of the year in 2025 - it's another superb release from one of Jamaica's most compelling voices.

French sound system champions Roll & Record reunite with Pili Boyo on the uplifting new 7" 'One By One', a heavyweight roots anthem produced by William Spring. Plus Roberto Sánchez and The 18th Parallel return via Fruits Records with 'Morning Blessing', the second taste of the forthcoming Showcase Vol. 2 album - a thunderous steppers workout recorded to 2-inch tape in Switzerland and Spain that celebrates gratitude and life's blessings.

And one of dancehall's greatest ever voices is back where he belongs. Buju Banton returns to VP Records after 23 years with his thirteenth studio album Too Too Bad, delivering the uncompromising hardcore dancehall sound that made 'The Gargamel' a legend. Four tracks from the new album feature in this week's edition.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Kasinda - This Life in DUB
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: The world premiere of the dub version of Naarm/Melbourne multi-instrumentalist Kasinda's debut single, 'This Life'. Written in Accra, Ghana and co-produced with Ghanaian producer Slim Drumz, the track pays tribute to African icons Kwame Nkrumah, Patrice Lumumba, Miriam Makeba and Yaa Asantewaa, while reflecting on the world we leave for future generations.

One of grime's most respected producers, Silencer, returns with his biggest project yet. 'Through Ball' unites an all-star lineup featuring Chip, Kruz Leone, Hitman Hyper, Bruza, Frisco, JME, P Money and D Double E over a club-ready instrumental blending classic grime with UK garage. The viral beat became one of the year's most anticipated grime releases before it was even recorded.

Plus, nuff roots reggae rarities, including an exclusive dubplate of The Meditations' 'Nah Give Up', mixed by Roberto Sánchez at Lone Ark Studio in Spain.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Rapid fyah from Koffee
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: Koffee gives a first taste of her forthcoming album, due in November, with two tracks - ‘Summer Fruits’ and ‘Rapid Fyah’ featuring Skillibeng.

Roll Deep return with new grime from Best In The Game Mixtape. ‘Entourage’ gets a spin from the new project by the legendary UK grime crew.

The Thompson Sound x Dubquake Records series heads back into the vaults, with Joe Yorke joining O.B.F on record for the first time on ‘Danger In My Eyes’. The track unearths a 70s reggae gem and rebuilds it in the O.B.F studio.

Also remembering Errol ‘Barkwood’ Brown, founding member, lead singer and percussionist of Bristol roots reggae legends Black Roots, who passed away unexpectedly on July 28. Formed in St Pauls in 1979, Black Roots helped establish Bristol as one of the great centres of UK roots reggae. Riddim Yard pays tribute with ‘Bristol Rock’.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Sean Paul stands on business
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: The Sleng Teng riddim rides again! Sean Paul teams up with the mighty King Jammy for 'Stand On Business', breathing new life into the groundbreaking digital dancehall riddim that changed Jamaican music forever in 1985.

Also new from Roll & Record, 'Forward Again' pairs Natto with William Spring on an original riddim inspired by the sounds and aesthetics of the 1980s - vintage vibes with a modern production and plenty of soundsystem weight.

Plus up-to-the-times dancehall with Silk Boss on 'Mery Macka', produced by CJTheChemist & Abroad Boss, and Prince Swanny coming heavy with 'Buss Head'.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Global Warming
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: 'Global Warming' - a raw, analog dubplate-style tune recorded at Attic Roots Studio in 2024, tackling the increasingly impossible-to-ignore reality of climate change. Released exclusively on Bandcamp as a free download, with a simple message - play it, spread it and help raise awareness.

Also three cuts on the mighty 'Morning Blessing' riddim from Fruits Records. Roberto Sánchez leads the way as Lone Ark with 'Morning Blessing', joined by New York deejay JonnyGo Figure's 'Love Life' and the Horns of Guiding Star Orchestra with the instrumental 'Hornsmen Blessing'. The riddim was recorded to 2-inch tape between Geneva and Cueto, with Sánchez also at the controls for the mixes and dubs.

Plus up-to-the-times dancehall from Jahvillani with '2019', Skillibeng on 'Zapper', and Popcaan with 'Unlocked'.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Unreleased Wayne Smith - first recording
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: Digging into the vaults for Wayne Smith’s previously unreleased ‘Zarro’ - his first-ever studio recording, cut at Channel One in 1980 with Prince Jammy and mixed at King Tubby’s. The tune rides the same steppers riddim as Lacksley Castell’s ‘What A Great Day’, with a Jammy dub on the flip.

Also revisiting Johnny Clarke’s heavyweight 1980 LP Originally Mr. Clarke, produced by Bunny ‘Striker’ Lee and newly restored and remastered. Pure roots business featuring ‘Bad Days Are Going’, ‘Blood Dunza’ and ‘Every Knee Shall Bow’, backed by an all-star crew including Sly Dunbar, Robbie Shakespeare, ‘Family Man’ Barrett, ‘Santa’ Davis, Earl ‘Chinna’ Smith and Tommy McCook.

Plus new dancehall from Jahvillani with two fresh cuts - ‘Mawd’, and a link-up with Skippa on ‘False Teeth’.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Enkutatash: Gift Of Jewels
item.description:
Celebrating Ethiopian New Year this week with The Abyssinians, including selections sung in Amharic - drawing on the Ethiopian language and imagery that runs deep through their music.

Also fresh productions from Riddim Yard favourite Roberto Sánchez. Spanish roots band Irregular Roots bring the heavyweight ‘Think It Twice’, recorded live and to tape at A-Lone Ark Muzik Studio, with Roberto producing, recording and mixing. The tune is exclusive to their new Jah Love 12".

And Ras Teo links again with Roberto Sánchez for ‘Long Time’, a new roots 7" on Jah Temple Records. Roberto produced, recorded and mixed the tune, backed by Lone Ark Riddim Force, with a dub version on the flip.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: LISTEN. Unknown T
item.description:
UK drill heavyweight Unknown T returns with his new album LISTEN., pushing beyond straight drill while keeping the cold delivery and unmistakable voice that made his name.

Back to 2002 with Zumjay’s ‘Courtney’ for Penthouse - a tribute to Jamaican cricket legend Courtney Walsh. The fearsome fast bowler formed one of the great West Indies partnerships with Curtly Ambrose and became the first man to take 500 Test wickets, holding the world record until Shane Warne passed him.

And right back to 1960 with Keith & Enid - Keith Stewart and Enid Campbell - alongside Trenton Spence & His Group on ‘Worried Over You’. Released on Blue Beat, it’s a beautiful slice of early Jamaican music from the R&B era just before ska took hold.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: A Serious Thing
item.description:
Killer new Horace Andy from A Serious Thing, the new double LP on Gorgon Records collecting 20 Bunny ‘Striker’ Lee productions, including Riddim Yard favourites ‘Zion Gate’, ‘Don’t Try And Use Me’ and ‘You Are My Angel’, with heavyweight mixes from King Tubby.

Keeping it up to the times with new dancehall from Skillibeng and his latest track ‘General’, plus some classic grime from Ocean Wisdom ahead of his upcoming Australian tour.

And something very different - ‘Waak Waak’ by New Sound of Ramo, traditional manikay - Yolŋu songlines - sung in the Jinang language. From the Marrangu people and their homeland of Walka, the song is about Waak Waak, the black crow dreaming, and roaring thunder before the wet season. The riddim comes from a DEB Players tune, with the singers laying the traditional song over the top.

Finally, paying tribute to legendary Jamaican bass player Clifton ‘Jackie’ Jackson, who died this week aged 79. From Duke Reid’s Supersonics and classics by Alton Ellis and The Melodians to ‘Israelites’, ‘The Harder They Come’ and decades with Toots & The Maytals, Jackie’s bass is all over the foundations of Jamaican music.
item.author: Rick Howe
